title: Inside an electric race car.
short: Accumulator monitoring, CAN diagnostics, and vehicle integration with Terrier Motorsport.
label: TERRIER MOTORSPORT
problem: Monitor an FSAE electric vehicle’s accumulator and integrate its charging, drivetrain, and safety systems.
contribution: I commissioned and configured Orion BMS2 for accumulator monitoring and charge/discharge control. During vehicle bring-up, I diagnosed faults using CAN traffic, event logs, and BMS history.
system: The BMS monitors the accumulator and participates in vehicle safety and charging control. I also configured and tested the DTI motor controller and CAN integration across the accumulator, drivetrain, and safety systems.
testing: Vehicle bring-up involved reviewing CAN traffic and BMS histories and coordinating with embedded, accumulator, powertrain, safety, and mechanical teams.
result: Commissioned and configured Orion BMS2 and completed motor-controller configuration and integration testing. Detailed measurements and engineering documentation are still to be added.

title: Keeping the bus in check.
short: A dual-controller CAN watchdog, from prototype to a custom PCB.
label: EMBEDDED SYSTEMS
problem: Monitor multiple vehicle CAN messages and check that the monitoring controllers themselves remain responsive.
contribution: I built a CAN watchdog using STM32/ESP32 and transceivers, implemented dual-controller heartbeat self-checks, and moved the prototype to a custom PCB.
system: Vehicle messages pass over CAN to the monitoring electronics. Dual-controller heartbeat checks provide a separate check on controller responsiveness.
testing: Detailed test cases, timeout settings, and failure-injection results have not yet been added to this notebook.
result: The prototype was moved to a custom PCB. Schematics, firmware excerpts, and validation records are still to be added.

title: A conversation made of light.
short: Transmitter and receiver PCBs, designed, built, and tested as one system.
label: HARDWARE / COMMUNICATIONS
problem: Build a working optical link and understand how distance and alignment affect the connection.
contribution: I personally designed and built the transmitter and receiver PCBs, integrated the complete hardware, and tested the system.
system: A transmitter sends a signal through an optical path to a receiver. This diagram illustrates that relationship; it is not a circuit schematic.
testing: I validated the MVP across distance and alignment conditions. Exact distances, component choices, and measurements are still to be documented.
result: Delivered a functional MVP with performance validated across distance and alignment conditions.

problem: Explore how embedded systems sense, communicate, and control physical behavior.
contribution: My in-progress ESP32 projects span RTOS multitasking, hardware interrupts, I²C sensor interfaces, Wi-Fi/UDP telemetry, Node.js dashboards, and PID-based robotic navigation.
system: Sensor data feeds embedded tasks, with telemetry available to a dashboard and control logic driving navigation. This is an illustrative overview of the areas under exploration.
testing: Work is in progress. Test procedures, tuning notes, and iteration records will be added as the projects develop.
